item: One liveness probe, never a signal on Windows; waits that ran to their timeout (row 98)
summary: On Windows CPython's os.kill is TerminateProcess, so the uninstall watcher's os.kill(pid, 0) ended the server it waited for (a -wal could be left) before erasing. src/pid_probe.pid_alive is the one probe: OpenProcess(SYNCHRONIZE)+WaitForSingleObject(0) on Windows, signal 0 on POSIX (zombie = gone), any doubt = running. The watcher embeds its source (spawn refuses without it), self_update and the panel call it, apply_update keeps a test-pinned byte-identical copy; a ratchet forbids any other os.kill(..., 0). Exact-timeout waits from #2052's slow report: crypto_erase 60 s = this bug; three restore-swap 300 s = Windows by nature (a held handle blocks replace), marked POSIX-only with a stepped-clock Windows contract test; law spelling = slow schema builds, now a copied template; help_md_lists 60 s = node fed the manual on stdin, now a file; article_indexes 62.5 s = not an exact timeout, unconfirmed.
